name: Acquired Factor VII Deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Acquired Factor VII Deficiency Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Prolonged prothrombin time (PT) not corrected by mixing studies
Reduced factor VII activity levels in coagulation assays
Exclusion of congenital factor VII deficiency and other coagulopathies
Detection of factor VII inhibitors (autoantibodies) in plasma
Clinical evidence of bleeding disproportionate to other causes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Prolonged PT not corrected by mixing studies plus reduced factor VII activity with exclusion of congenital causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Detection of inhibitors supports diagnosis but is not always present.

pathognomonic.notes: Includes epistaxis, gum bleeding, and easy bruising
searchTerms: bleeding from mucous membranes without injury
spontaneous bleeding in mouth or nose

pathognomonic.symptomName: Prolonged bleeding after minor trauma or surgery
searchTerms: long bleeding after minor injuries or surgery

common.notes: Joint bleeding leading to swelling and pain

searchTerms: tiredness due to low blood count
autoimmune symptoms like rash and joint pain
immune system attacking body causing rash and arthralgia

laboratory: Prolonged prothrombin time (PT) with normal activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT)
Presence of factor VII inhibitors detected by Bethesda assay or mixing studies
imaging: Imaging to identify bleeding sites such as CT for intracranial hemorrhage or ultrasound for abdominal bleeding
genetic: No genetic mutations as this is an acquired disorder
other: Clinical bleeding manifestations disproportionate to other coagulation parameters

distinguishingFeatures: Correction of PT with vitamin K administration

redFlags: Sudden onset of severe bleeding without prior history
Prolonged PT not corrected by mixing studies
Intracranial hemorrhage or other life-threatening bleeding
references: Franchini M, Lippi G. Acquired factor VII deficiency: a systematic review. Blood Transfus. 2010;8(2):82-87.
Orphanet: Acquired factor VII deficiency - ORPHA599495
Katz U, et al. Acquired factor VII deficiency: clinical and laboratory features. Haemophilia. 2013;19(4):e230-e237.
